s: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 is called the “Mini-Constitution” primarily because it:
o: replaced the parliamentary form of government with a presidential form
introduced the system of judicial review in India
abolished the office of the President
made sweeping changes in several parts of the Constitution
x: The 42nd Amendment is known as the “Mini-Constitution” because of its wide-ranging and sweeping changes to the Constitution.
tq: Choose the option that explains the famous title rather than merely naming an associated provision.
sec: 42nd Amendment - words added to the Preamble, year, "Mini-Constitution"  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976:
1. It was enacted during the Emergency of 1975–77.
2. It was enacted under the leadership of Indira Gandhi.
3. It was the Second Amendment of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the relevant amendment was the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, not the Second Amendment.
tq: Split the options by identifying the wrong amendment number in the confusable statement.

s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
o: Abolition of the power of judicial review in its entirety
Freezing of delimitation of parliamentary seats
Addition of new Directive Principles of State Policy
x: The 42nd Amendment curtailed judicial review and attempted to exclude it in certain matters, but it did not abolish the power of judicial review in its entirety.
tq: Find the extreme statement that goes beyond the stated effect of the amendment.
sec: 42nd Amendment - words added to the Preamble, year, "Mini-Constitution"  [APPSC]

s: Which case struck down the provisions of the 42nd Constitutional Amendment that sought to give Parliament unlimited amending power and exclude judicial review?
x: In Minerva Mills (1980), the Supreme Court struck down the clauses of the 42nd Amendment that attempted to confer unlimited amending power on Parliament and exclude judicial review.
tq: Match the constitutional consequence with the correct Supreme Court case.
sec: 42nd Amendment - words added to the Preamble, year, "Mini-Constitution"  [APPSC]

s: In the Berubari Union case, the Supreme Court held that the Preamble:
o: was an integral part of the Constitution and could be amended under Article 368
formed the basic structure and could not be referred to for interpretation
was not a part of the Constitution, but could guide interpretation where an Article was ambiguous
was enforceable by constitutional courts as a source of legislative power
x: In the Berubari Union case (1960), the Preamble was held not to be a part of the Constitution, although it was regarded as a key to the minds of the framers and an aid to interpretation in cases of ambiguity.
tq: Separate the case’s holding on constitutional status from its limited interpretative use.
sec: Is the Preamble part of the Constitution - Berubari, Kesavananda, LIC; enactment, legal effect, enforceability  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of the Kesavananda Bharati judgment on the Preamble?
o: It held that the Preamble was enforceable independently of the Fundamental Rights.
It reaffirmed that the Preamble was not part of the Constitution.
It held that the Preamble was part of the Constitution and could be amended, subject to the basic structure limitation.
It held that the Preamble was part of the Constitution and could not be amended in any circumstance.
x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) overruled the Berubari position by recognizing the Preamble as part of the Constitution. It may be amended under Article 368, but its basic structure cannot be destroyed.
tq: Distinguish amendability from the limitation imposed by the basic structure doctrine.
sec: Is the Preamble part of the Constitution - Berubari, Kesavananda, LIC; enactment, legal effect, enforceability  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Berubari Union — 1960
2. Kesavananda Bharati — 1973
3. LIC of India — 1995

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: Berubari Union was decided in 1960, Kesavananda Bharati in 1973 and LIC of India in 1995. All three pairs are correctly matched.
tq: Use the year as the anchor and verify each case-year pair independently.
sec: Is the Preamble part of the Constitution - Berubari, Kesavananda, LIC; enactment, legal effect, enforceability  [APPSC]

s: The Supreme Court in LIC of India (1995) described the Preamble as:
o: an enforceable code of administrative conduct
a source of independent legislative power
an integral part of the Constitution
x: The LIC of India judgment (1995) recognized the Preamble as an integral part of the Constitution.
tq: Identify the later judicial position rather than the earlier Berubari view.
sec: Is the Preamble part of the Constitution - Berubari, Kesavananda, LIC; enactment, legal effect, enforceability  [APPSC]

s: Which statement regarding the enactment of the Preamble is correct?
o: It was added by the Constituent Assembly after the commencement of the Constitution.
It was enacted before the remaining provisions of the Constitution.
It was enacted after the rest of the Constitution had already been enacted, so that it would fit the constitutional text.
It was enacted simultaneously with the Objectives Resolution in 1946.
x: The Preamble was enacted after the rest of the Constitution had been enacted, enabling it to conform to the constitutional text.
tq: Test the sequence of enactment rather than the date of commencement.
sec: Is the Preamble part of the Constitution - Berubari, Kesavananda, LIC; enactment, legal effect, enforceability  [APPSC]

s: A court is interpreting an ambiguous constitutional provision. Which role may the Preamble properly perform in such a situation?
o: It may independently create a new legislative power.
It may serve as an aid to interpretation.
It may invalidate every law inconsistent with any Preamble ideal.
It may be enforced as a separate fundamental right.
x: The Preamble may guide courts in interpreting ambiguous constitutional provisions. It is neither an independent source of legislative power nor an enforceable set of rights.
tq: Apply the interpretative role of the Preamble to an ambiguity-based scenario.
sec: Is the Preamble part of the Constitution - Berubari, Kesavananda, LIC; enactment, legal effect, enforceability  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements about the legal effect of the Preamble:
1. It is not a source of power for the legislature.
2. It is not a limitation on powers expressly granted by the Constitution.
3. It is non-justiciable.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The Preamble does not confer legislative power, does not limit powers expressly granted by the Constitution, and cannot be directly enforced by a court.
tq: Check each statement against the distinct legal effects of the Preamble.

o: It assures liberty of movement, residence, occupation and worship.
It assures equality of income, status and political representation.
It assures liberty of action and equality of rights.
It assures liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship, and equality of status and opportunity.

s: Which one of the following best expresses the constitutional meaning of the term ‘Sovereign’ in the Preamble?
o: The Union alone exercises power over all subjects without constitutional limitations
India has a hereditary head of State with unrestricted powers
India accepts the foreign policy decisions of the Commonwealth of Nations
India is free from internal and external control and can frame its own foreign policy
x: ‘Sovereign’ means that India is internally and externally free, is not subject to external control and can determine its own foreign policy.

s: The term ‘Socialist’ in the Preamble signifies which of the following?
o: Democratic socialism with coexistence of public and private sectors
A completely State-owned economy based exclusively on Marxism
A free-market economy without State intervention
An economy based exclusively on Gandhian village industries

s: Which of the following correctly explains the significance of the Supreme Court’s decision in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) in relation to the Preamble?

It declared that Parliament could not amend any part of the Preamble.

s: Which of the following statements best reflects the relationship between the 1976 insertion of the word ‘Secular’ and the basic structure doctrine?
o: Secularism was part of the basic structure even before the word was inserted in the Preamble.
The 42nd Amendment removed secularism from the basic structure and retained it only in the Preamble.
Secularism was excluded from the Constitution until the Supreme Court recognised it in 1994.
Secularism became part of the basic structure only because the word was inserted in 1976.
x: The constitutional position stated in the material is that secularism was part of the basic structure even before the word was inserted in 1976.
tq: Separate the textual insertion of a word from the pre-existing constitutional principle it expresses.

s: Which one of the following was a criticism of the insertion of certain words into the Preamble during the Emergency?

The insertions were made by the Supreme Court without parliamentary approval.
